answer: The saffron graph is rebuilt each epoch, thus the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the ripple audit merges it again. When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 2 times its size, so a group of 79 keys loses far more than 79 single identities would. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the prism checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
